transcript.text:
*settles into chair, adjusting papers on the table and looking directly at Lincoln with a measured, businesslike expression*

Mr. Lincoln, we appreciate you taking the time to meet with this panel today. Your speeches have certainly garnered attention — the party talks about little else these days. But let us be candid with one another, as frank men must be when the stakes are this high.

*leans forward slightly*

You've lost elections before. The Senate race in '55, your Congressional bid — Douglas is a formidable opponent, perhaps the most formidable in the nation. So I must ask you this directly: Tell us about a time when your political judgment proved wrong. A position you took publicly that you now wish you hadn't, or a campaign decision that cost you dearly. 

*pauses, maintaining steady eye contact*

And more importantly — how did you handle it? We need to know what kind of man we're placing our confidence in when the inevitable setbacks come.

Gentlemen, I appreciate your candidness and your concerns. It is true that I have faced defeats in the past, and I do not shy away from acknowledging them. In the election for the U.S. Senate in 1855 and in my Congressional bid, the outcome was not in my favor.

One particular instance that comes to mind is the Kansas-Nebraska Act. At that time, I believed it was necessary to compromise on the issue of slavery in the territories. Looking back, I see now that my position was flawed. I came to realize that there can be no compromise on the fundamental principle that all men are created equal.

When faced with the consequences of my misjudgment, I did not retreat or make excuses. Instead, I learned from my mistakes and used them to shape my future actions. I redoubled my commitment to the cause of justice and equality, and I continued to work tirelessly towards those ends.

I understand the importance of resilience in the face of adversity, and I assure you that I am prepared to confront any challenges that may come our way. I believe that my experiences have only strengthened my resolve and my dedication to the principles that guide our party.
